title: Orchestrator pod ignores JOB_KUBE_TOLERATIONS for itself
body:
### What method are you using to run Airbyte?

Kubernetes

### Platform Version or Helm Chart Version

0.50.1

### What step the error happened?

During the Sync

### Revelant information

Setup: Kubernetes, orchestrator enabled, JOB_KUBE_TOLERATIONS set.

Behavior: sync jobs run with correct tolerations, but an orchestrator pod starts without tolerations on its pod. Env variables inside an orchestrator pod are correct.

Expected behaviour: orchestrator runs with tolerations from JOB_KUBE_TOLERATIONS env variable.

Tolerations are not set: https://github.com/airbytehq/airbyte-platform/blob/28e2339679bbb2235f3c317b6c8cd843f222092a/airbyte-commons-worker/src/main/java/io/airbyte/workers/process/AsyncOrchestratorPodProcess.java#L451C45-L451C45

### Relevant log output

_No response_

comments.author: brianbolt
comments.body:
I am facing the same outcome with a new version helm chart `0.442.3` (AIrbyte 0.67.17).  Orchestrator pods cannot be scheduled because the tolerations are not passed to the pod.

WIth this yaml:
```
global:
  jobs:
    kube:
      nodeSelector:
        "disco/node-type": "jobs-node"
      tolerations:
        - key: "airbyte-jobs"
          operator: "Exists"
          effect: "NoSchedule"
```

When the pod spins up the tolerations have the following (missing the `airbyte-jobs` key):


```
  tolerations:
  - effect: NoExecute
    key: node.kubernetes.io/not-ready
    operator: Exists
    tolerationSeconds: 300
  - effect: NoExecute
    key: node.kubernetes.io/unreachable
    operator: Exists
    tolerationSeconds: 300
```

The node selecter however is passed to the orchestrator pod:


```
  nodeSelector:
    disco/node-type: jobs-node
 ```
 
 This causes the pod to not get scheduled with the following error:
 
 ```
0/4 nodes are available: 1 node(s) had untolerated taint {airbyte-jobs: true}, 3 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/4 nodes are available: 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling
  ```

comments.author: alexremn

Still no tolerations in 0.64.3.

Seems like related to absence of toleration spec [here](https://github.com/airbytehq/airbyte-platform/blob/main/airbyte-workload-launcher/src/main/kotlin/pods/factories/OrchestratorPodFactory.kt) (im not a kotlin dev, so could be wrong).

comments.author: andrevus
comments.body:
There is a workaround available using a Kyverno policy that automatically adds the required Tolerations to Pods based on conditions such as labels or namespaces. This ensures the correct Tolerations are applied without needing to modify every Pod manifest manually. However, I’m still waiting for a fix from the Airbyte team to address the issue directly. Here’s an example of the Kyverno policy:
```
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: add-default-tolerations-airbyte
spec:
  rules:
    - name: add-tolerations-if-not-exist
      match:
        resources:
          kinds:
            - Pod
          namespaces:
            - airbyte
      preconditions:
        all:
          - key: "{{ request.object.metadata.labels.sync_step || '' }}"
            operator: Equals
            value: "orchestrator-replication"
      mutate:
        patchStrategicMerge:
          spec:
            tolerations:
              - key: "example-key"
                operator: "Exists"
                effect: "NoSchedule"
```

comments.author: brentonmorris
comments.body:
I am attempting to use this to set the tolerations for the provisioner:
https://github.com/airbytehq/airbyte-platform/blob/main/charts/airbyte/values.yaml#L965-L969

Is this the correct way to get `tolerations` and `nodeSelector` specs onto the job pods that workload-launcher creates?

I must not be getting the format of my string correctly. I get this error:

```
Error: cannot patch "airbyte-workload-launcher" with kind Deployment: Deployment.apps "airbyte-workload-launcher" is invalid: spec.template.spec.containers[0].env[29].valueFrom: Invalid value: "": may not be specified when `value` is not empty
```

The data I am passing to `extraEnv`:
```
extraEnv = [
  {
    name  = "JOB_KUBE_TOLERATIONS"
    value = "effect=NoExecute,key=node_type,value=worker;effect=NoExecute,key=provisioner,value=${local.cluster_provisioner_name}"
  }
]
```

Does anyone know if this is supposed to add `tolerances` and `nodeSelector` to the job pods provisioned by workload-launcher?

comments.author: amardatar

@brentonmorris I'm doing it via global.jobs.kube in the helm chart instead, like this:

```yaml

  jobs:
    kube:
      nodeSelector:
        {key}: {value}
      tolerations:
        - key: {key}
          operator: Equal
          value: {value}
          effect: NoSchedule
```

Which seems to be working - I haven't tried using `extraEnv` (although I vaguely remember seeing it so maybe it should work).

comments.author: AcidFlow
comments.body:
Hello!

We are running into the same issue, as previously described it happens on v1.1.0 and using the nightly build indeed propagates the value correctly.

Looking at the diff between main and v1.1.0, I think the commit that fixes the issue is the following one:

https://github.com/airbytehq/airbyte-platform/commit/2ca3c4192793b15a1ccc2bfd644dd725c3a2903c#diff-3555dc77946bb010495d4a97b3060553f759452f781e0f5b54b3c8a37394c3b0R227

**Edit**

We internally rebuilt an image based on v1.1.0 with cherry picked `2ca3c4192793b15a1ccc2bfd644dd725c3a2903c` and used it as our workload-launcher image. Now we do get the tolerations correctly propagated to the pods launched by workload-launcher.
